questions.question: You’re waiting in line at the café, and the person in front of you drops their bag. What would be the most appropriate response if you wanted to help without being too direct?
options: Oh dear, I’m so sorry about that! I’ll get it for you.
That’s okay, it’s not my problem.
You should really be more careful with your belongings.
I’m sure you’ll find it soon enough.
questions.answer: Oh dear, I’m so sorry about that! I’ll get it for you.

questions.question: Your friend says, ‘I think we should move this meeting to the afternoon.’ How would you respond if you wanted to suggest an alternative time?
options: Yes, that’s a great idea!
I disagree—we should stick to the original time.
How about we try 3 PM instead?
You’re wrong; afternoon is too late.
questions.answer: How about we try 3 PM instead?

questions.question: Your colleague says, ‘I’ve been meaning to ask you—when is the best time to start the new project?’ What would be the most polite way to offer your opinion?
options: I think we should start next Monday, but we should confirm with the team.
Next Monday is fine, but we should wait for the manager’s approval.
No, we can’t start yet—it’s too rushed.
The project should start tomorrow, but that’s not possible.
questions.answer: I think we should start next Monday, but we should confirm with the team.

questions.question: At a formal dinner, someone says, ‘I’ve heard a lot about your new book.’ How would you politely express your opinion about it?
options: Oh, it’s just a draft—I haven’t finished it yet.
I’m not sure if it’s good enough to publish.
It’s very interesting, but I’m not a writer, so I can’t really say much.
I disagree with the title—it’s misleading.
questions.answer: It’s very interesting, but I’m not a writer, so I can’t really say much.

questions.question: Your boss asks, ‘Did you receive the report from the client?’ You want to politely ask for clarification. What would you say?
options: Yes, I’ve already sent it back to them.
I’m not sure what you mean by ‘the report from the client.’
I’ll get it right away—what exactly did they ask for?
The report was sent yesterday, but I haven’t checked it yet.
questions.answer: I’m not sure what you mean by ‘the report from the client.’
